cass: Quick bug report — when using @redwood/sdk from a pnpm workspace into our edge app (Cloudflare Worker) we hit two separate problems: the worker bundle fails with module-not-found at runtime, and VSCode complains about missing types. Installing the published package works fine.

vijay: Typical pnpm/workspace symlink vs published layout mismatch. Can you paste the SDK package.json (the one in the package root, not dist)?

cass: Sure (simplified):
```json
{"name":"@redwood/sdk","version":"0.3.1","main":"dist/index.cjs.js","module":"dist/index.esm.mjs","types":"dist/index.d.ts","exports":{"import":"./dist/index.esm.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs.js"}}
```
Our monorepo uses pnpm-workspace.yaml with packages: ["packages/*"]. Editor error: "Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/sdk'" even though dist/index.d.ts exists after build. Worker bundler logs: `Error: Cannot find module '@redwood/sdk'` during runtime bundling.

maya: A couple things we've seen: (1) pnpm symlinks can expose the source package.json, not the one you'd publish — bundlers sometimes use the wrong manifest; (2) many bundlers treat symlinked workspace packages as external unless you set preserveSymlinks:false. Which bundler are you running?

cass: esbuild via our CI deploy step. We did try setting preserveSymlinks:false which made the worker bundler include the package code, but the TS/VSCode still resolved types to the workspace root and refused to pick up dist d.ts.

vijay: For TS server in monorepos we usually add two things: (A) postbuild copy of package.json into dist (postbuild: cp package.json dist/package.json) so local consumers see the same manifest as published, and (B) `typesVersions` map in package.json so tsserver prefers dist types: "typesVersions": {"*": {"*": ["dist/*"]}}. I know it's messy but it stabilizes editor behavior.

cass: We tried adding a typesVersions entry and copying dist/package.json — editor fixed locally. But CI worker still intermittently dropped authorization headers when our SDK retried failed requests (only in ESM/edge build). We had retry logic that did req.clone() and re-fetched. In node it was fine, in the worker the Authorization sometimes vanished leading to 401s on retry.

maya: Edge runtimes often implement Headers and Request differently. clone() semantics aren't always identical. Safer approach: on retry create a fresh Request and copy headers explicitly: `new Request(orig.url, { method: orig.method, headers: new Headers(orig.headers), body: orig.body })`. Also make sure the body is buffered for retries (streams are one-shot).

vijay: Another subtlety: if your bundler resolves to the source (src) instead of dist, you might be shipping a different retry helper or a dev polyfill that behaves differently in edge. That's why copying dist/package.json helps — it forces bundlers/readers to treat the package like a published artifact.

cass: Good point — switching to the dist/package.json layout also made the bundler pick the compiled retry helper which used the explicit header copy. That fixed the auth header loss in staging.

rowan: Two extra notes from our experience: (1) export `types` inside `exports` for better tool support: e.g. "exports": {"import": {"default":"./dist/index.esm.mjs","types":"./dist/index.d.ts"}, "require": {"default":"./dist/index.cjs.js","types":"./dist/index.d.ts"}} — not all tools read it but it's helpful; (2) add a small examples/monorepo that demonstrates pnpm+esbuild+CF with preserveSymlinks:false and a CI job that builds it; that catches regressions early.

maya: Also if you have internal consumers doing deep imports like `@redwood/sdk/lib/foo` and your `exports` only exposes the top-level, upgrade path is either to add explicit subpath exports or provide a compatibility re-export at the top-level (and mark it deprecated). Deep imports will break under stricter resolvers like PnP or newer bundlers.

cass: We're not deep-importing currently, but good to know. Ok action items: I'll open a tiny PR to add postbuild copying of package.json into dist, add typesVersions, include `types` in exports, and adjust the retry helper to explicitly copy headers and buffer JSON bodies. Also add an examples/monorepo + CI build.

vijay: Sounds perfect. If you want, I can review the example and help add the CI matrix (pnpm + yarn classic + yarn berry) so we surface env-specific issues.

cass: Thanks! Opening PR now and linking back here.

lint-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/610 to track monorepo+edge resolution and added label: devex.

rowan: TL;DR: pnpm symlinks + exports + types and edge Request/Headers differences are the triplet. Fixes: dist/package.json in build, typesVersions, `types` in exports, preserveSymlinks:false for bundlers, and explicit header-copy retry logic with buffered bodies.

cass: Appreciate the help — will follow up with PR link and CI preview. :rocket:
